cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Sedimentary rocks form from the accumulation and lithification of sediment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Clastic sedimentary rocks are classified by grain size: clay-shale, silt-siltstone, sand-sandstone, gravel-conglomerate/breccia

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Chemical sedimentary rocks form by precipitation from solution: limestone, rock salt, gypsum

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Biochemical sedimentary rocks form from biological activity: chalk, coal, bioclastic limestone

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Lithification involves compaction (squeezing out water) and cementation (minerals precipitating in pore spaces to bind grains)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sedimentary Rocks
cards.back: Sedimentary structures like bedding planes, graded bedding, cross-bedding and ripple marks reveal the depositional environment
